key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation leads to different solid-state conversion pathways in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap tuning must be controlled differently for each absorber.
engineering_relevance: This enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells with high efficiency and improved thermal stability, supporting scalable manufacturing.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compared solid-state conversion in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Used absorber design guided by bandgap-specific conversion behavior
evidence_signal: The paper reports a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell with 19.2% power conversion efficiency and 80% average efficiency retained after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: The solid-state conversion pathway is highly sensitive to precursor thickness, composition, and vertical diffusion, so process control must be tight to avoid compositional gradients or bandgap drift.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
